interpretation_boundary: SLSA 1.2 and in-toto Attestation 1.2 define the evidence fields and verifier checks. The authors define this admission state machine, conflict escalation rule, precedence, and labels. An ALLOW decision is not a SLSA certification.

action_semantics.ALLOW: Admit the artifact at the requested verified build level, or retain an already admitted artifact whose basis remains valid.
action_semantics.HOLD: Keep a candidate out of the protected release channel because required attestation evidence is absent or insufficient.
action_semantics.DEMOTE: Remove an admitted artifact from the protected release channel because its recorded admission basis no longer satisfies the policy.
action_semantics.ESCALATE: Quarantine the artifact and require incident review because authenticated evidence conflicts on a policy-critical field.

boolean_checks.source_basis: SLSA verification begins by verifying the attestation signature.
in-toto validation rejects an envelope with no recognized attester.
in-toto validation requires the versioned Statement type.
SLSA and in-toto verification bind the attestation subject to the artifact digest.
SLSA verification requires the SLSA provenance predicate type.
The verifier checks builder identity against its roots of trust and local expectations.
Artifact verification may require the expected source repository.
Artifact verification may require the expected source branch, tag, or immutable revision.
SLSA provenance records external parameters in the build definition.
The provenance run details describe the execution that produced the artifact.
SLSA verification summaries can bind the policy resource and its digest.

level_check.source_basis: SLSA build levels are cumulative; admission requires a verified level at least as high as the requested level.
